parts.title: A Smaller Home
parts.text: When the factory closed in 1931, Clara's family learned what **adversity** truly meant. Her father could no longer pay the rent on their house, so they moved into a cramped **tenement**. The stairwell smelled of damp wood, and the single bathroom down the hall was shared by six families. Clara's mother tried to hide her worry, but anyone could see the **plight** of parents with three children and no steady wages.

parts.title: Making Do
parts.text: Clara's brother Walter, only ten, grew **forlorn** when he had to **relinquish** his bicycle to a pawnbroker for grocery money. Their father, a **stoic** man who rarely complained, simply patted the boy's shoulder. Some families in the neighborhood lived in real **squalor**, with broken windows and rats in the halls, and Clara felt thankful for what little her own family had. Meals became **austere**: bread, beans and one pot of soup stretched across three days.

parts.title: The Neighbor Downstairs
parts.text: Odessa, the elderly woman on the first floor, was a **stalwart** friend to everyone in the building, always ready to lend a cup of flour or a warm coat. Clara's mother taught the children to be **prudent**, saving every button, scrap of string and penny in a tin. When a letter finally confirmed that the factory would not reopen, Walter muttered that all his hoping had been **futile**. Odessa found **solace** in her old hymns, and that evening she began to sing in the stairwell until the whole building hummed along.

parts.title: What Remained
parts.text: Their troubles did not end quickly. Work returned slowly, a day here and a week there, and money stayed scarce for years. Still, Clara noticed that the hardest season had taught her something no classroom could. People survive difficult times by leaning on one another. Decades later, she kept one button from that old tin on her desk as a reminder.

definitions.meaning1: Bearing pain or hardship calmly, without showing emotion or complaining. Example: The stoic hiker kept walking despite her blisters.

definitions.meaning1: Comfort during a time of sadness or disappointment. Example: Reading gave her solace after a long, hard day.

definitions.meaning1: To give up or let go of something, often unwillingly. Example: The champion had to relinquish her title after the injury.

definitions.meaning1: Loyal, strong and dependable. Example: The stalwart volunteer worked every Saturday for ten years.
definitions.meaning2: A loyal and hardworking supporter. Example: The stalwarts of the club attended every meeting.

Their meals were _(7)_, mostly bread and beans. The family learned to be _(8)_ with money, never spending a penny without thinking.
